identity: Front matter plus the first pages of an Arabic translation of a French popular-science pocket book. The opening lines are title-page fields, one per <NL>: the series line ثمرات من دوحة المعرفة (= Les Petites Pommes du Savoir), the author فرانسوا كيبيس (Francois Kepes), the title البيولوجيا التركيبية هل هي أقوى من الطبيعة with the French original La biologie de synthese plus forte que la nature set under it, and the translator credit ترجمة د فريد الزاهي. Then a section heading ما الذي نعنيه بالبيولوجيا التركيبية, two paragraphs of expository definition, one long paragraph carrying a worked hypothetical example (a small firm's engineer building a circadian-clock circuit for an insulin pump, in a four-stage model/simulate/build/test loop), then a second heading المنهج والمبادئ المنظمة and the start of the methodological summary. Register = translated expository nonfiction written for a general reader, so §B/§L rules apply but with a shorter unit than encyclopedia prose. The source is OCR'd (Ia for la, قاعد for قاعدة, a column break splitting تصويب from ثوابت) and a footnote reference 2 has survived in the token stream.
law: The unit is the printed full stop of the Arabic translation, plus every layout line and the title-page question mark. Measured on the stretches where the reading is not in doubt, this text's sentence runs about 14 to 25 tokens - shorter than the 25-45 of encyclopedic prose, because the French source is written in short declarative sentences for a broad audience, and the translator has followed it clause for clause. Default is WELD. The cut licences I allow myself here, in descending order: (1) <NL> and the final token, free; (2) an ASYNDETIC clause opener - a clause that begins with no connective at all after a completed predication (إن, يتضمن, سيتبنى, بالجملة, بشكل أدق, من جهة ثانية, لنفترض) - in Arabic running prose clauses inside one sentence are welded by و/ف/ثم or a subordinator, so bare juxtaposition is the strongest evidence of a stop that survives punctuation stripping; (3) a fronted frame that carries its own main clause (ولأن...فإن, وإذا ما...فإنه, ما إن...حتى, وانطلاقا من, ولكي, وهكذا, ومع ذلك فـ, وبهذا المعنى); (4) a cohortative لنأخذ / لنستشهد / لنفترض; (5) وقد + perfect; (6) an anaphoric summarising subject NP (وهذا الأمر). Nothing else cuts. Bare و and ف and ثم, حيث, بحيث, كما, لأن, أو, trailing relatives, comma lists, appositive glosses, Latin-script title lines, numbers and the footnote marker all weld.
